events.title: Abel Tasman Sights Van Diemen's Land
events.description: Dutch explorer Abel Tasman, sailing for the Dutch East India Company, became the first known European to sight the island later named Tasmania. He called it Van Diemen's Land.
events.significance: The sighting added a new landmass to European maps of the southern hemisphere. The island was later renamed Tasmania in Tasman's honor.

events.title: Darwin's On the Origin of Species Is Published
events.description: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species went on sale in London, and its first print run sold out almost at once.
events.significance: The book set out the theory of evolution by natural selection. It changed biology and reshaped how people understand life on Earth.

events.title: Lee Harvey Oswald Is Shot on Live Television
events.description: Two days after the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, Oswald was shot by Jack Ruby while police were transferring him. The shooting happened in front of a live television audience.
events.significance: Oswald's death meant he never stood trial. It left lasting questions and fueled decades of debate about the Kennedy assassination.

events.title: Freddie Mercury Dies
events.description: Queen's lead singer died in London at age 45, one day after publicly confirming that he had AIDS.
events.significance: Mercury was one of rock's most dynamic performers. His death brought wider attention to the AIDS crisis, and Queen's music is still hugely popular.

events.title: Birth of Philosopher Baruch Spinoza
events.description: Baruch Spinoza was born in Amsterdam to a Portuguese-Jewish merchant family. He became one of the leading thinkers of the early Enlightenment.
events.significance: His writings on God, nature, ethics and freedom of thought influenced later philosophy, science and secular politics.
